# Spec

## Problem

Finding the range of a collection with `lo` takes two calls, `Min` and `Max` in `find.go` (or `MinBy` and `MaxBy`), and so two passes over the data. For a slice that is wasteful; for an `iter.Seq` in package `it` it is worse, because a sequence may be expensive to produce or impossible to iterate twice. `MinBy` and `MaxBy` also take comparison functions with opposite meanings, so asking for both extremes of the same ordering needs two different callbacks. There is no helper that returns both extremes in one pass.

## Scope

Add a "min and max in one pass" family in three parts that build on each other.

Part 1, core helpers in `find.go`: `MinMax` for ordered values, `MinMaxBy` for any type with one `less` comparison function used for both extremes, and `MinMaxByErr` whose comparison function can fail. Each walks the slice once and returns the minimum first and the maximum second. An empty collection gives zero values. When several elements tie for an extreme, the first of them in the collection is returned, for the minimum and for the maximum alike. `MinMaxByErr` stops at the first error and returns zero values with it. Tests go in `find_test.go`.

Part 2, iterator helpers in `it/find.go`: `MinMax` and `MinMaxBy` over `iter.Seq[T]`, with the same results as the core helpers for the same elements, consuming the sequence exactly once. Tests go in `it/find_test.go`. There is no iterator `Err` variant, as for `it.MinBy`.

Part 3, examples, documentation and benchmarks for both packages: `Example` functions in `lo_example_test.go` and `it/find_example_test.go`, `README.md` index lines and sections for the core helpers, five new `docs/data/` pages with links added to the eight existing `Min`/`Max` pages, lines in both the core and the iterator lists of `docs/static/llms.txt`, and benchmarks in `benchmark/core_find_bench_test.go` and `benchmark/it_find_bench_test.go`.

All new functions are appended at the end of their file (`find.go` after `SamplesBy`, `it/find.go` after `SamplesBy`) with no change to either import block, so the line numbers existing `docs/data/*.md` pages record in `sourceRef` do not move. Core code uses nothing newer than Go 1.18.

## Non-goals

- Index-returning variants (`MinMaxIndex`, `MinMaxIndexBy`), time variants in the style of `Earliest`/`Latest`, and `it.MinMaxByErr`.
- `mutable`, `parallel` or `exp/simd` variants.
- Changing `Min`, `Max`, `MinBy`, `MaxBy` or any other existing helper, including the reversed comparison convention of `MaxBy`.
- Reimplementing `Min` or `Max` on top of the new helpers.
- Special handling of `NaN` or of comparison functions that are not a strict weak ordering.
- `// Play:` links and `playUrl` values: the helpers are not released, so the playground cannot compile them.
- Editing any `sourceRef` of an existing page, and adding README sections for the `it` helpers (the README documents core helpers only).

## Affected services and packages

Package `github.com/samber/lo` gains three exported functions in `find.go`, with tests in `find_test.go` and examples in `lo_example_test.go`. Package `github.com/samber/lo/it` gains two exported functions in `it/find.go`, with tests in `it/find_test.go` and examples in `it/find_example_test.go`. Package `benchmark` gains benchmarks in `benchmark/core_find_bench_test.go` and `benchmark/it_find_bench_test.go`. Documentation changes are in `README.md`, `docs/static/llms.txt`, the new pages `docs/data/core-minmax.md`, `docs/data/core-minmaxby.md`, `docs/data/core-minmaxbyerr.md`, `docs/data/it-minmax.md` and `docs/data/it-minmaxby.md`, and the existing pages `docs/data/core-min.md`, `docs/data/core-max.md`, `docs/data/core-minby.md`, `docs/data/core-maxby.md`, `docs/data/it-min.md`, `docs/data/it-max.md`, `docs/data/it-minby.md` and `docs/data/it-maxby.md`. No dependency or existing signature changes.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `find.go` declares, after every existing declaration in the file and in this order, exactly `func MinMax[T constraints.Ordered](collection []T) (T, T)`, `func MinMaxBy[T any](collection []T, less func(a, b T) bool) (T, T)` and `func MinMaxByErr[T any](collection []T, less func(a, b T) (bool, error)) (T, T, error)`, and the import block of `find.go` is unchanged.
2. `MinMax` in `find.go` returns the smallest element first and the greatest second: `MinMax([]int{3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6})` is `1, 9`; `MinMax([]int{7})` is `7, 7`; `MinMax([]int{3, 2, 1})` and `MinMax([]int{1, 2, 3})` are `1, 3`; `MinMax([]int{-2, -7, -1})` is `-7, -1`; `MinMax([]string{"pear", "apple", "zebra"})` is `"apple", "zebra"`; `MinMax([]float64{-1.5, 2.5, 0})` is `-1.5, 2.5`; `MinMax([]time.Duration{time.Hour, time.Second, time.Minute})` is `time.Second, time.Hour`.
3. `MinMax`, `MinMaxBy` and `MinMaxByErr` in `find.go` return the zero value of `T` twice (and a nil error for `MinMaxByErr`) when the collection is empty or nil: `MinMax([]int{})` and `MinMax([]int(nil))` are `0, 0`.
4. `MinMaxBy` in `find.go` treats `less(a, b)` as "a is ordered before b" for both results: with `less` comparing `len(a) < len(b)`, `MinMaxBy([]string{"s1", "string2", "s", "string3"}, less)` is `"s", "string2"`.
5. `MinMaxBy` and `MinMaxByErr` in `find.go` return, among several elements equal to the smallest, the first in the collection, and among several equal to the greatest, also the first in the collection: for elements with keys and ids `{2,"a"}, {1,"b"}, {3,"c"}, {1,"d"}, {3,"e"}, {2,"f"}` compared by key the result ids are `"b", "c"`; for `{5,"x"}, {5,"y"}, {5,"z"}` they are `"x", "x"`; for `[]string{"bb", "aa", "cccc", "dddd", "cc"}` compared by length the result is `"bb", "cccc"`.
6. `MinMaxBy` and `MinMaxByErr` in `find.go` never call `less` for a collection of zero or one element; a one-element collection returns that element twice.
7. `MinMaxByErr` in `find.go` returns the same two values as `MinMaxBy` and a nil error when `less` never fails. When `less` returns a non-nil error, `MinMaxByErr` returns the zero value of `T` twice and that same error (`errors.Is` holds), and does not call `less` again.
8. `it/find.go` declares, after every existing declaration in the file and in this order, exactly `func MinMax[T constraints.Ordered](collection iter.Seq[T]) (T, T)` and `func MinMaxBy[T any](collection iter.Seq[T], less func(a, b T) bool) (T, T)`, and the import block of `it/find.go` is unchanged.
9. `MinMax` and `MinMaxBy` in `it/find.go` return, for a sequence yielding the elements of a slice in order, exactly what `MinMax` and `MinMaxBy` in `find.go` return for that slice, for every case of criteria 2 to 6, including zero values for an empty sequence, the first-of-equals rule for both results, and no call of `less` for a sequence of zero or one element.
10. `MinMax` and `MinMaxBy` in `it/find.go` range over the sequence exactly once and to its end: for a sequence that counts how often it is started and how many items it yields, `MinMax` over the items `4, 8, 1, 6` returns `1, 8` after one start and four yields.
11. The doc comment of each of the five functions starts with its name, says that the minimum and the maximum are found in a single pass, and says what is returned for an empty collection. Those of `MinMaxBy` (both packages) and `MinMaxByErr` also say that `less` reports whether `a` is less than `b` and that the first of several equal smallest values and the first of several equal greatest values are returned. That of `MinMaxByErr` also says that iteration stops at the first error, which is returned. Those in `it/find.go` also contain the line `// Will iterate through the entire sequence.` None has a `// Play:` line.
12. `find_test.go` has functions `TestMinMax`, `TestMinMaxBy` and `TestMinMaxByErr`, and `it/find_test.go` has functions `TestMinMax` and `TestMinMaxBy`. Each calls `t.Parallel()` and uses `assert.New(t)`. Between them they cover criteria 2 to 7 for the core helpers and criteria 9 and 10 for the iterator helpers, including an empty input, a one-element input, ties for both extremes, and the error path of `MinMaxByErr`.
13. `lo_example_test.go` has, immediately after `ExampleMaxIndexByErr` and in this order, `ExampleMinMax`, printing the two results of `MinMax([]int{3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6})` with `"%d %d"` under `// Output: 1 9`; `ExampleMinMaxBy`, printing the two results of `MinMaxBy([]string{"s1", "string2", "s", "string3"}, ...)` compared by length with `"%s %s"` under `// Output: s string2`; and `ExampleMinMaxByErr`, printing with `"%v"` the error of a `MinMaxByErr` call over the same slice whose `less` returns `errors.New("s is not allowed")` when `a == "s"`, under `// Output: s is not allowed`. `it/find_example_test.go` has, immediately after `ExampleMaxIndexBy` and in this order, `ExampleMinMax` and `ExampleMinMaxBy` with the same inputs wrapped in `slices.Values` and the same output comments. No example declares a variable named `min` or `max`.
14. `benchmark/core_find_bench_test.go` has, immediately after `BenchmarkMaxIndexBy` and in this order, `BenchmarkMinMax` and `BenchmarkMinMaxBy`: each loops over `lengths`, builds `ints := genSliceInt(n)`, and runs a sub-benchmark named `strconv.Itoa(n)` calling `lo.MinMax(ints)` or `lo.MinMaxBy(ints, func(a, b int) bool { return a < b })`. `benchmark/it_find_bench_test.go` has, immediately after `BenchmarkItMaxBy` and in this order, `BenchmarkItMinMax` and `BenchmarkItMinMaxBy`: each loops over `itLengths`, builds `ints := genInts(n)`, and runs a sub-benchmark named `fmt.Sprintf("ints_%d", n)` calling `it.MinMax(ints)` or `it.MinMaxBy(ints, func(a, b int) bool { return a < b })`.
15. `README.md` lists `- [MinMax](#minmax)` and `- [MinMaxBy](#minmaxby)`, in this order, on the lines after `- [MaxIndexBy](#maxindexby)`, and has sections `### MinMax` and `### MinMaxBy`, in this order, between the end of the `### MaxIndexBy` section and `### Latest`. `### MinMax` states the single pass and the empty-collection result and shows `lo.MinMax([]int{3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6})` as `1, 9` and `lo.MinMax([]int{})` as `0, 0`. `### MinMaxBy` states the meaning of the comparison function and the first-of-equals rule, shows the length comparison over `[]string{"s1", "string2", "s", "string3"}` as `"s", "string2"`, and has a second Go code block introduced by the comment `// Use MinMaxByErr when the comparison function can return an error` showing a `lo.MinMaxByErr` call and its result `"", "", error("s is not allowed")`. Neither section has a `[[play](...)]` line.
16. `docs/data/core-minmax.md`, `docs/data/core-minmaxby.md` and `docs/data/core-minmaxbyerr.md` exist, each with front matter `name` (`MinMax`, `MinMaxBy`, `MinMaxByErr`), `slug` (`minmax`, `minmaxby`, `minmaxbyerr`), `sourceRef: find.go#L<line of that func declaration>`, `category: core`, `subCategory: find`, an empty `playUrl:`, `variantHelpers` holding only its own key (`core#find#<slug>`), `position` (`390`, `400`, `410`), and `signatures` holding only, respectively, `"func MinMax[T constraints.Ordered](collection []T) (T, T)"`, `"func MinMaxBy[T any](collection []T, less func(a T, b T) bool) (T, T)"` and `"func MinMaxByErr[T any](collection []T, less func(a T, b T) (bool, error)) (T, T, error)"`. Their `similarHelpers` are, in order: for `MinMax`, `core#find#min`, `core#find#max`, `core#find#minmaxby`, `core#find#minmaxbyerr`, `iter#find#minmax`; for `MinMaxBy`, `core#find#minby`, `core#find#maxby`, `core#find#minmax`, `core#find#minmaxbyerr`, `iter#find#minmaxby`; for `MinMaxByErr`, `core#find#minmaxby`, `core#find#minmax`. Each page ends with a short description and a Go code block showing a call and its result.
17. `docs/data/it-minmax.md` and `docs/data/it-minmaxby.md` exist, each with front matter `name` (`MinMax`, `MinMaxBy`), `slug` (`minmax`, `minmaxby`), `sourceRef: it/find.go#L<line of that func declaration>`, `category: iter`, `subCategory: find`, an empty `playUrl:`, `variantHelpers` holding only its own key (`iter#find#<slug>`), `position` (`630`, `640`), and `signatures` holding only, respectively, `"func MinMax[T constraints.Ordered](collection iter.Seq[T]) (T, T)"` and `"func MinMaxBy[T any](collection iter.Seq[T], less func(a T, b T) bool) (T, T)"`. Their `similarHelpers` are, in order: for `MinMax`, `core#find#minmax`, `iter#find#min`, `iter#find#max`, `iter#find#minmaxby`; for `MinMaxBy`, `core#find#minmaxby`, `iter#find#minby`, `iter#find#maxby`, `iter#find#minmax`. Each page ends with a short description and a Go code block showing an `it.` call and its result.

One entry is added as the last entry of the `similarHelpers` list, with no other change, in each of: `docs/data/core-min.md` and `docs/data/core-max.md` (`  - core#find#minmax`), `docs/data/core-minby.md` and `docs/data/core-maxby.md` (`  - core#find#minmaxby`), `docs/data/it-min.md` and `docs/data/it-max.md` (`  - iter#find#minmax`), `docs/data/it-minby.md` and `docs/data/it-maxby.md` (`  - iter#find#minmaxby`).

## Risks

- `README.md`, `docs/static/llms.txt` and `lo_example_test.go` are edited by other helper additions in flight. The insertion points above are specific to the find helpers so that the changes merge cleanly; inserting elsewhere invites conflicts.
- The tie rule for the maximum is easy to get wrong: updating the maximum with `!less(item, max)` returns the last of several equal greatest values and fails criterion 5. The maximum changes only when `less(max, item)` holds.
- `MinMaxBy` deliberately uses one `less` function for both results, unlike `MaxBy`, whose callback means "greater". Callers who pass a `MaxBy`-style callback get the two results swapped; the doc comments, README and docs pages must spell out the meaning of `less`.
- Part 2 must not collect the sequence into a slice and call the core helper: that satisfies the values but defeats the purpose for large or unbounded-cost sequences. Criterion 10 checks the single pass, not the allocation.
- `it/` files carry `//go:build go1.23`; the core helpers in `find.go` are also compiled by Go 1.18 and may not use `min`, `max`, `cmp` or `slices`.
- Examples and tests that name a variable `min` or `max` shadow Go built-ins and trip the repository's `predeclared` lint rule.
- The docs site's `sourceRef` values are line numbers. Appending at the end of `find.go` and `it/find.go` keeps the existing ones valid; placing the functions beside `Min` and `Max` would silently make every later `sourceRef` in those files stale.
